title: Capacity Sprint Ops: Reservoir & Fastpath Autoscale Guidance
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Quarterly roadmap slice to design, pilot, and operationalize a two-pronged autoscale model for Dedicated pools: 1) a small persistent reservoir to absorb short bursts without expensive immediate provisioning; and 2) a fastpath hedging mechanism that enables sub-minute ephemeral capacity brings with predictable cost envelopes. The goal of this initiative is to reduce p99 latency regressions during burst windows, smooth monthly committed spend, and improve customer confidence for short-lived load spikes. This ticket captures product scope, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and dependencies for the Q2 pilot.
objectives: Reduce p99 tail latency for dedicated pools during burst events by 30% in the pilot(versus baseline)
Decrease incremental monthly committed spend volatility for pilot customers by 20%
Deliver a working pilot to 3 internal customers and 2 external beta customers by end of Q2
Create a concise console UX and API knobs for reservoir size, fastpath budget, and degradation policy
milestones: 2026-03-15: Finalize product spec and acceptance criteria
2026-04-05: ENG designs for reservoir autoscaler and fastpath cold-start API complete
2026-04-22: Prototype implementation merged; internal perf tests kicked off
2026-05-10: Internal pilot with 3 teams; iterate based on feedback
2026-05-30: External beta rollout to 2 customers and launch monitoring dashboards
acceptance_criteria: Reservoir keeps warm capacity for short bursts without triggering full pool scaling for events <= 90s in test harness
Fastpath provisioning reaches usable capacity within 45s and recovers without impacting steady state SLOs
Console exposes reservoir size and fastpath budget with guardrails; API supports per-pool overrides
End-to-end metrics (latency, tokens/sec, cost delta) are visible in Console with per-customer breakdown
Runbook documented for on-call to triage reservoir fill/fallthrough and revert policies
metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency during bursts (baseline vs pilot)
percent of bursts absorbed by reservoir (no scale event)
delta in committed GPU hours and egress cost per customer
customer satisfaction for beta customers (NPS-style feedback)
rollouts: Alpha: internal-only pools with synthetic burst tests (April)
Beta: opt-in by 2 external customers with SLA guardrails (May)
Gradual: enable default reservoir for low-risk tiers if beta metrics meet targets (June, out of scope for this ticket)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Reservoir may increase baseline cost if overprovisioned -> Mitigation: conservative default size, automated shrink after low-util windows
Risk: Fastpath cold-start failures under extreme contention -> Mitigation: circuit-breaker that falls back to reservoir or degraded model variant
Risk: Console UX complexity leading to misconfiguration -> Mitigation: ship guarded presets and inline guidance, require manager approval for >X size
Risk: Interference with Dedicated autoscale policies -> Mitigation: clearly define precedence and provide simulation tooling prior to enablement
